decision: Suggestions are filtered to what the shopper can actually get: in stock, in their size, near them
why: A suggestion that is out of stock or not in your size feels smart and sells nothing.
value: Every suggestion is buyable, which is the only kind that counts.

decision: The trade-off is drawn as a race on one 0–5 s axis, both lanes labeled illustrative targets
why: Speed is felt, not read; two lanes on one clock make 4.8 s of blank screen visible to anyone.
alternative: A bullet list of performance techniques.
value: A non-technical founder sees why the frontend work matters.

decision: AI fills a reserved, fixed-height slot with an 800 ms timeout and a cached fallback
why: The page must be useful before the AI answers, and a late answer must never move what the shopper is reading.
alternative: Wait for the AI before rendering.
value: Useful at 0.6 s, CLS 0, and suggestions whenever they are ready.

decision: 2,000 products in 24-item pages with opaque cursors and a stable sort key, published as static files
why: Cursor pages stay fast at any depth, and static files make the demo cost nothing to serve.
value: A real, measurable demo on the free tier.

decision: About 20 rows exist in the page and are recycled as you scroll, with heights reserved
why: Drawing 2,000 rows costs memory and frames; the shopper only ever sees seven or eight at once.
value: Scrolling stays smooth however far you go.

decision: The bought fitting room opens only after a size is chosen
why: Each try-on is billed; gating on a size spends it on shoppers close to buying.
alternative: Offer try-on on every product page.
value: The cost of the feature tracks intent, not traffic.
